newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 1996 trade surplus at US$14 billion.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 1996 trade surplus at US$14 billion.

text.p: Taiwan's trade surplus was US$14 billion in 1996, the highest level since 1990, the state-funded Central News Agency quoted officials as saying on Sunday.
The island's exports hit US$116.1 billion in 1996, while imports were at $102.1 billion, the agency reported.
The economics ministry plans to release the trade data officially on Tuesday.
In December 1996, Taiwan's exports rose a year-on-year 12 percent to $10.4 billion and imports were up 5.5 percent from December 1995 to $8.4 billion.

The central bank, in a year-end package of projections for the coming year, said on December 31 that Taiwan could expect 1997 exports to grow 8.39 percent, up from an official 1996 full-year forecast of 6.80 percent.
The island's imports are expected to grow 7.34 percent in 1997, up from 1996's forecast of 4.11 percent, the central bank said.
